Named for Leopold Bloom, built for New York.

With a nod to James Joyce’s Ulysses

The story behind the sign

A neighborhood tavern with a literary soul.

Bloom’s opened its doors in October 2013. Its name honors Leopold Bloom, the everyday hero at the center of James Joyce’s Ulysses—a fitting patron for a place made for conversation, company and a generous welcome.

Come for a fireside cocktail, settle in for the game, or take over the upstairs room. Private and corporate events can host up to 120 people.

Yes. There is always room for another story.

One room, many moods

at home.
